runtime host arm — remote-runtime panes are a real execution host, and a host type that cannot name them forces callers to lie

round-trips the system-default route

INVARIANT 2 — CANONICAL ROUND-TRIP: this parses cleanly to accountId `a@b` but is not what formatRouteKey emits, so it is REFUSED. Accept it and a unique index on target_route_key holds two rows for one subscription, and one reservation is claimed twice
and the canonical spelling of that same route IS accepted — the rejection above is about the spelling, not the route
canonical round-trip, lowercase-hex spelling: `%2f` decodes to `/` but re-encodes to `%2F`, so it is a second spelling of one route and is refused
canonical round-trip, over-escaped spelling: `%2D` decodes to `-`, which encodeURIComponent leaves unreserved, so this too is a second spelling
canonical round-trip, encoded-blank distro: it normalizes to the default distro, re-formats to bare `wsl`, and so cannot be a route key of its own

canonical round-trip, BOM distro: U+FEFF is whitespace to JS `trim`, so the distro blanks out and the key re-formats to bare `wsl` — a port using Rust's `char::is_whitespace` (which excludes U+FEFF) would ACCEPT this second spelling of the default distro

the same trim mismatch in the other direction: U+0085 (NEL) is whitespace to Rust and NOT to JS, so this IS a distro and the route is accepted — a port trimming it would refuse a key the TS side issues
not a string — route keys arrive from SQLite and CLI flags, so a non-string is a rejection, never a coerced fallback
empty

unknown account tag — `borrowed` is not an account kind, and guessing at one names someone else's subscription
empty managed id — a managed route with no account is not a route
unknown host kind
empty host body — `ssh:` names no target
no host at all
malformed escape in the account — decodeURIComponent THROWS, and a throw at the caller is not a decision, so it is caught into a rejection
truncated multi-byte escape in the host
malformed escape in the provider
two hosts spending ONE subscription are two routes — the host is part of the identity, not a decoration
equality is decided on the canonical form, so a blank distro and the default distro are ONE route
health may be account-scoped: the host is dropped so an exhausted subscription is not reported healthy merely because another host has not hit it yet
same subscription, different host — the SAME scope string as the case above
but two accounts of one provider stay separate — dropping the host must not drop the account
order-independent and deduped, so one store has one key however a launch happens to enumerate it
a trailing separator is the SAME directory — reporting these as disjoint would let a drain proceed while a live CLI still holds the store
a bare root stays usable: stripping its only separator would leave a surface with no path at all
the real darwin launch: config dir + auth file + BOTH the scoped and the legacy keychain item, ordered by the formatted surface so the string is a stable SQLite value
a path containing the grammar's own `|` and `:` is escaped, so the joined key stays parseable
round-trips the darwin launch key
the EMPTY string is the empty store, not a parse failure — a launch that mutates no credential surface is a real state, and it must collide with nothing
not a string
unknown surface kind — a store whose surfaces we cannot name cannot be checked for collisions, so it is refused rather than half-read
a keychain item missing its account half: service alone does not name an item
a config-dir with an extra part is not something formatStoreKey ever emitted (the path is escaped, so it cannot contain a raw `:`)
malformed escape rejects instead of throwing at the caller — store keys come back from SQLite
INVARIANT 1 (half one): two launches with different config dirs are NOT equal...
INVARIANT 1 (half two): ...yet they OVERLAP, because they fight over one keychain item. An equality-shaped port runs these concurrently and corrupts that credential
genuinely disjoint stores coexist — the predicate must not be a blanket refusal either
the darwin LEGACY keychain item a config-dir-only key would miss: different config dirs, and the collision is only visible because the store names every surface
an empty store collides with nothing — otherwise a launch that touches no credential would block every drain
trailing separator: `/home/u/.claude/` and `/home/u/.claude` are one directory and therefore one collision
case is NOT folded: on Linux these are two stores, and over-merging would report a collision that does not exist and stall a rotation
INVARIANT 3: a rotation is a multi-key transaction, so the saga locks the union of every store it touches. Lock only the config dir and the keychain item it also rewrites is unguarded
the union of two overlapping stores dedupes, so the shared surface is locked once and the key stays canonical
the union of nothing is the EMPTY store, which collides with nothing — locking nothing must not read as locking everything
a described launch commits, and the persisted form is exactly the two keys plus the pane identity
no runtime — an unattributed pane stays unattributed rather than acquiring a plausible-looking binding
no incarnation — without one a respawn cannot be detected, so the binding would be an audit answer nobody can check
the incarnation-id cap is 128 units and this is exactly 128 — both sides must agree where the boundary is
one unit over the cap is refused — a cap the two sides place differently is a cap that admits a binding on one side only
two incarnations of ONE pane are two bindings — a respawn ends one binding and commits another, it never edits in place
the same pane described in a different surface order is ONE binding — equality reads the canonical keys, not the caller's spelling
round-trips a persisted row
an EMPTY store key is the empty store, so the row still deserializes — the distinction from an absent key is the next case
an ABSENT store key is a rejection, not the empty store — a row that never recorded what it was touching must not read as touching nothing
a route key that is not canonical is not a route — the same refusal parseRouteKey makes, reached through the persistence path
an unreadable store key is a rejection rather than a binding with a guessed-at store
a row with no incarnation cannot be checked against a respawn, so it is refused
a non-string runtimeId is refused rather than coerced — persisted state is untrusted input
null is not a binding
only LIVE panes that touch the store block a drain; the live pane on another config dir does not
an ENDED incarnation does not block, even though its store still overlaps — liveness is the runtime's answer, and the drain waits on processes, not on history
INVARIANT 1 at the drain seam: a live pane whose store only PARTIALLY overlaps still blocks, because it holds the same keychain item the drain is about to rewrite

DIVERGENCE FOUND: a persisted ptyIncarnationId that is a JSON NUMBER. `String(raw.ptyIncarnationId ?? '')` coerces it to "5" and the binding COMMITS — a port that types the field as a string rejects the row, leaves a live pane unattributed, and lets a store-scoped drain proceed while that pane still holds the store
the same coercion for a non-integer number — "1.5", not a rejection
a boolean coerces to "true", which is a legal incarnation id — the coercion is String(), not a type check
an object coerces to "[object Object]" — absurd, but it is what the persisted path accepts, and a port must agree or the two disagree about which panes exist
an empty array coerces to the EMPTY string, which is not a legal incarnation id — rejected, unlike the number above
a non-empty array joins to "a,b" — the array arm of String(), pinned so the seam cannot half-model the coercion
explicit null hits the `?? ''` and is REJECTED — the arm that agrees, kept beside the ones that did not

DIVERGENCE FOUND: two rows share (runtimeId, ptyIncarnationId) but differ in liveness and in store. Liveness is the caller’s answer PER BINDING; a harness that rebuilds it from that pair marks the dead row live and reports a drain as blocked that is not

the same collision the other way round: the row that touches the drained store is the DEAD one, so nothing blocks. A set of live pairs is a union, so it can only ever widen liveness — it answers "blocked" for both arrangements and is wrong in both
differs ONLY by store — two panes at the same incarnation cannot be spending different credential stores, and dropping this conjunct kept the old corpus green
differs ONLY by route — system-default and a managed account are different subscriptions, and this conjunct was unreached too
differs ONLY by runtimeId — the last of the four conjuncts
the provider is percent-encoded too. No vector had a provider needing it, so a port that emitted the provider raw stayed green — and a raw `/` there makes the grammar ambiguous
and it round-trips: the encoded provider is the only spelling parseRouteKey accepts
the raw spelling of that same provider is NOT a route key — it splits at the first `/`, so it names provider "a"
encodeURIComponent leaves ~!*'()-_. unreserved. Dropping `~` from that set kept the corpus green, and it would make every tilde-bearing key re-spell itself

lowercase hex escapes decode. parseStoreKey has NO canonical round-trip check (unlike parseRouteKey), so this is ACCEPTED and re-canonicalized to uppercase — a decoder that only read uppercase would reject a key SQLite happily holds
an escape that is not valid UTF-8 is a REJECTION, not U+FFFD. decodeURIComponent throws and the module catches it into null; a lossy decoder would mint a store key naming a path nobody asked for
a lone surrogate encoded as UTF-8 is refused for the same reason

a stored key that is out of order, carries a trailing separator, and duplicates a surface: parseStoreKey re-runs createStoreKey, so it comes back sorted, trimmed and deduped. Returning the parsed list as-is kept the corpus green, and it would let one store hold two keys
the same normalization on the construction path, so the two paths cannot drift
